newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won closes lower on forward dollar buying.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won closes lower on forward dollar buying.

text.p: The won closed slightly lower against the dollar on Thursday due to about $50 million worth of one-month forward dollar buying in late trading, dealers said.
But who bought in the forward trading were not clear, they said. "The central bank or companies were believed to have bought, but certainly not banks," said a foreign bank dealer.
Exporter deals and dollar sales ahead of the planned expansion of the foreign stockholding ceiling helped the won rise to a high of 891.90 earlier in the day, they said.
The won ended at 892.70 against Wednesday's closing and today's opening of 892.50. It touched a low of 892.90.
The foreign stock ownership limit will be raised on May 2 to 23 percent from 20 percent.
"The dollar appears to be undervalued in the forward trading," said a domestic bank dealer.
The won's mid-rate is expected to be pegged at 892.30 on Friday, compared with 892.60 today.
Dealers said trading would range from 892.00 to 893.50 on Friday.
